title: Chapter 1 Quiz 1
description: Start here: what an algorithm is, what it must do, and why we write one.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: Which sentence describes an **algorithm** best?
options: A finite sequence of clear steps that solves a problem
A programming language used to write instructions
An endless sequence of clear steps that solves a problem
A part of the computer that stores the instructions
questions.explanation: An algorithm is a finite sequence of instructions that solves a problem. Watch out: it must end after a finite number of steps, so an endless sequence is not an algorithm.
questions.hint: Think of a recipe: ordered steps that lead to a result and then stop.

questions.question: Following a cooking recipe is an example of an algorithm.
questions.explanation: A recipe is an ordered set of clear steps that produces a result and ends: exactly what an algorithm is.

questions.question: Which of these are **characteristics** of an algorithm?
options: Every instruction is clear and unambiguous
It always requires data to be entered
It ends after a finite number of steps
It produces at least one result
It must be written in the Pascal language
questions.explanation: An algorithm is definite (clear steps), finite (it terminates) and gives at least one output. Watch out: input is optional, and the language does not matter.

questions.question: Match each characteristic to its meaning.
right: The algorithm may or may not need data to start
The algorithm gives at least one result
Every instruction is clear and unambiguous
The algorithm ends after a finite number of steps
questions.explanation: These are the four characteristics from the course: input, output, definiteness and finiteness.

questions.question: An algorithm is a {{1}} of steps that solves a problem, and it must {{2}} after a finite number of steps.
questions.explanation: An algorithm is an ordered sequence of steps, and it must terminate (finiteness).

questions.assertion: An algorithm must stop after a finite number of steps.
questions.reason: A procedure that never stops never gives its result.
questions.explanation: Both are true, and the reason explains why finiteness is required: a result is only obtained if the steps end.

questions.question: Why is it useful to write an algorithm **before** writing the program?
options: It makes the computer run the program faster
It removes the need to test the finished program
It replaces the work done by the compiler
It structures the logic and gives repeatable results
questions.explanation: Algorithms help to structure the problem-solving logic, to use time and memory well, and to get the same result each time.

questions.question: Which of these is an algorithm?
options: Steps to withdraw cash at an ATM, then stop
The name of the program shown on the screen
A list of the ingredients needed to bake a cake
Press the bell, then repeat these steps forever
questions.explanation: Clear steps that end with a result form an algorithm. Watch out: a list of ingredients has no steps, and a procedure that repeats for ever never gives a final result.

questions.question: An instruction sequence that needs no input data at all cannot be an algorithm.
questions.explanation: An algorithm may or may not require input. Watch out: the course says the input is optional, but at least one output is required.
